sylabus.polecenie:
Each item is ONE course card ("COURSE SYLLABUS AND SPECIFICATION", it starts with "Curriculum title:"). Skip the cover and any page that is not a course card.
code: the course code (e.g. EFZ214AIJ3432_3S). The course title is printed as "English title (polish title)" with the group in parentheses on the next line, e.g. "(PODSTAWOWE)": en = the English part, pl = the Polish part with the first letter capitalised (when both are the same, repeat it), group = the group without parentheses (PODSTAWOWE, KIERUNKOWE, OGÓLNOUCZELNIANE, ANOTHER TO PASS ...).
elective = true only when the course status is "elective". unit = the text after "Unit:" (e.g. "Lecture in the humanities [moduł]"), else "".
forms: one row per form of instruction in the hours table, f = W (lecture), CW (discussion classes), LAB (laboratory), KON (conversation), SEM (seminar), WF (PE classes); h = number of hours; c = type of credit exactly as printed (e, pg, p ...); s = semester number. hours = the Total hours, ects = the ECTS total.
coord and inst: people as printed, but names written in capitals get normal capitalisation ("dr hab. TOMASZ BERNAT" -> "dr hab. Tomasz Bernat"); inst = list of instructors.
goals = course/module objectives, pre = prerequisites (omit "none", "brak", "-"), how = modes of delivery: paragraphs as printed, wrapped lines joined with one space; leave out the standard paragraph that starts "The course teacher shall specify how artificial intelligence".
out: learning outcomes, c = category as printed (knowledge, skills, social competences), k = EP number (EP1 ...), t = the outcome text.
topics: every numbered topic of the CONTENT tables, in order, f = the form of that table (same codes as forms), t = topic text without its number, h = hours.
assess: assessment methods, m = method in lower case with the first letter capitalised, ep = the EP codes it checks.
grading = paragraphs of the grading criteria before the heading "Grade calculation principles", calc = paragraphs after that heading.
final: m = the final grade calculation method as printed (e.g. Arytmetyczna, Ważona), parts = one row per part: n = the part name in brackets (e.g. wykład, ćwiczenia), c = its credit type (e.g. egzamin, zaliczenie z oceną), w = its weight as printed ("1,00") or "" when there is none.
lit = basic reading, sup = supplementary reading: one entry per publication, wrapped lines joined.
load = the STUDENT WORKLOAD table rows in order, k = row label as printed, v = number.

przyklady.en: Supercinema: Film Philosophy in the Digital Age
przyklady.pl: Supercinema: filozofia kina w erze cyfrowej
goals: the course offers the theoretical frames helping participants understand how space, time, characters and our receptions of these concepts function in the digital cinema

out.t: Participants know and name the concepts of space, time etc. present in the analogue and digital cinema, and understand the ethical imperative/s behind them
Participants are capable of recognising the dependencies between the digital and analogue cinema
Participants are ready to discuss the questions vital for the digital cinema and use the knowledge of the medium transmedially

topics.t: Analogue vs digital cinema: similarities, differences, exchange
From Temporality to Time in Digital Cinema
Digital Film -Viewer-World: the Montage of Attractions

grading: The grade awarded for the final test is the grade awarded for the course.
calc: The final grade for the course is the lecture grade.
lit: Nicholas Rombes (2017): Cinema in the Digital Age, Wallflower Press
Thomas Elsaesser, Malte Hagener (2015): Film Theory. An Introduction Through the Senses, Routledge
sup: Stephen Prince (2019): Digital Cinema, Rutgers UP

plan.polecenie:
Each item is ONE class in the weekly timetable of one student group (one cell of the grid). The timetable has a page per group (e.g. C111).
grupa = the group number, tydzien = odd (tydzień nieparzysty), even (parzysty) or oba (every week), d = weekday: 0 Monday ... 4 Friday.
od/do = start and end time as H:MM (e.g. 8:15, 9:45). pl = Polish course name, en = English name when printed, else "".
k = form: W lecture/wykład, CW ćwiczenia, LAB laboratorium, K konwersatorium, S seminarium, X anything else (make-up classes, trainings).
p = the teacher with titles as printed, r = room as printed (e.g. "s. 002"), g = lab subgroup letter (A, B) or "", n = a note such as single dates ("Jednorazowo: 19.11.2026") or "".
When the same class is in both week tables, return it once with tydzien = oba.
